terminals.CAPTURE_DTCS: DTCs not captured yet. Pull and record codes from every module before anything else.
terminals.BATT_LOW: Battery or starting circuit is below spec under load. Fix charging and cabling first, then restart this flow.
terminals.SUPPLY_LOW: ECU supply is low. Trace the supply fuse, relay and wiring back to the source.
terminals.SUPPLY_HIGH: ECU supply is high. Check the charging system and the supply feed for a bad regulator.
terminals.GROUND_BAD: Ground fault found. Clean or replace the ground, clear codes, retest.
terminals.CAN_OUT_OF_SPEC: CAN termination is out of spec. Isolate modules one at a time to find the loading node.
terminals.COMMS_OK: Bus traffic present. Move on to fuel and ignition diagnosis with the captured DTCs.
terminals.COMMS_FAULT: No bus traffic at the probe point. Suspect the harness or a shorted node on the bus.

gates.title: DTCs captured
gates.instruction: Scan every module and write down all stored and pending codes. Do not clear anything.
gates.safeguard: Do not disconnect the battery or clear codes until every DTC is recorded.

gates.title: Battery voltage while cranking
gates.instruction: Meter across the battery posts, not the cable clamps. Crank for a few seconds and hold the lowest reading.
gates.safeguard: Measure at the posts so a bad clamp doesn't hide behind a good number.

gates.title: ECU supply, key on engine off
gates.instruction: Key on, engine off. Meter the ECU supply at the supply fuse or relay output. Don't pierce any wire.
gates.safeguard: Keep the key on and the engine off for this reading.

gates.title: ECU grounds corroded or loose
gates.instruction: Disconnect the battery, then inspect and wiggle-test every ECU ground. Is any ground corroded, loose or damaged?
gates.safeguard: DTCs must already be captured before the battery comes off.

gates.title: CAN-H to CAN-L resistance, key off
gates.instruction: Key off. Meter between CAN-H and CAN-L at the diagnostic connector.
gates.safeguard: Meter only. Do not bridge CAN-H and CAN-L.

gates.title: Bus traffic present at the sealed connector
gates.risk: Back-probing a sealed connector breaks the seal and can let water in, causing intermittent faults later.
gates.instruction: Back-probe the bus lines at the sealed connector with a scope or logger. Do you see traffic on the bus?
gates.safeguard: Reseal the connector with dielectric grease when you're done.
